newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1-day depos surge 3 points on reserve-end.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1-day depos surge 3 points on reserve-end.

text.p: Polish one-day rates surged three points at bid as banks were hungry for cash to square mandatory average reserve levels in the last days of November's reserve period, dealers said.
They said the market was likely to keep seeking cash until the end of the week and that the shortage might deepen if banks receive negative balances from the clearing house over the next few days.
"The rate jump comes from negative balances from the clearing house ahead of the reserve-end and it is likely to stay until Friday," said Marek Wieczorkiewicz from PKO BP.
At 0900 GMT both overnight and tomorrow/next rates were quoted at 23.00/25.00 percent, up from opening's 19.90/20.10 percent and early T/N bids of 20.00 percent respectively.
Dealers said that there was no active trade in longer deposits, which signalled the money market was drying.
They said the price jump was not a reaction to Tuesday's central bank comments that it may need to raise interest rates next year to curb swelling domestic demand.
"The money market is generally drying, and trade in longer-term cash is scarce," PKO's Wieczorkiewicz said.

The Polish zloty strenghtened against the basket of currencies and was quoted up against both dollar and mark despite a stable dollar/mark relation in European trade after some early currency-sales, dealers said.
They said the sales could be related to the shortage on the money market where banks could be cutting currency positions to gain zloty liquidity before the end of the November reserve.
The Friday value date for spot transactions is the last working day to square average reserves in November period, which ends on Sunday, December 1.

At 0945 GMT the zloty was quoted at 2.23/2.20 percent from the trading band centre, up from opening's 2.14/2.10 percent. It was at 2.8345/52 to the dollar, up from opening's 2.8370/85 and at 1.8584/89 to the mark, up from 1.8600/05.
